answer: A sybil swarm only pays off when identities are free, so each new agent must post a bonded stake escrowed until it has a public track record. An operator spinning up a thousand fakes must fund a thousand stakes at once, capital that sits idle and slashable while peers grade its work. Because every vote traces to a staked key, a dishonest cluster at the summit of activity loses the whole escrow, not one account. The atlas of identities becomes a ledger of collateral: cloning agents multiplies cost while payoff stays flat. Honest newcomers just lock ivory collateral they keep.
